title: Close the apply_patch bypass in bee-guard.ts
action: Slice judge found OpenCode 1.18.16 registers a fourth write-capable tool, apply_patch (write-group ["edit","write","apply_patch"] in the installed binary), which bee-guard.ts's switch never forwards — default: return null is a TypeScript-side allow, violating the every-decision-from-bee rule. Add the apply_patch case: tool id apply_patch, payload field patchText mapped onto the patch-body key bee's detectors read (tool_input keys ["input","patch","command"], detectors.rs:18-27; write_guard/main.rs:65 already matches the apply_patch name). Also: enumerate the installed binary's full write-capable tool registry in discovery.md so coverage claims rest on the registry, not on probe transcripts; fix discovery.md's 'forwarded verbatim' wording (it translates field names); soften the bee-guard.ts header comment that overstates undecidable-as-fail-closed (bee's own could-not-decide is fail-open by design, mod.rs:60-68). Live-probe an apply_patch deny in an opencode run session if the free provider cooperates; otherwise record the attempt and why it could not run.

truths: apply_patch reaches bee hook write-guard — no write-capable registered tool falls through to a TypeScript allow
The write-capable tool registry of the installed binary is recorded in discovery.md
The verbatim-forwarding wording and the fail-closed overstatement are corrected
An apply_patch deny probe ran, or its failure to run is recorded with the reason

trace.outcome: Mapped apply_patch to bee write-guard in bee-guard.ts; recorded the write-capable tool registry and corrected discovery.md wording
